positions.frame: what is the constitutive distinction between owning and renting one's intelligence, and what does each side of the opposition retain or commoditize?
positions.why: Both expressions perform the owned-vs-rented intelligence distinction as bedrock creed — unhedged, present-tense, aphoristic maxims arranged in matched opposition (owned/rented, commodity/asset-you-keep). Conviction reads both at principle level; register reads both as the same AphoristicTechnicalMaxim; value reads both as appealing to autonomy through self-origination of capability. The two clauses of src-3 extend the same opposition from intelligence itself to its substrate and perspective, deepening rather than diverging from src-2's core distinction.
